skill.name: managing-branches
skill.description: Plan and automate Git branch workflows for Gitflow, GitHub Flow, trunk-based development, releases, hotfixes, and worktrees.
skill.summary: Manage Git branch strategy, naming, flow validation, release branches, hotfixes, and worktrees.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, Git worktree path examples, localhost URLs, and dictionary configuration access. Real risks remain in the executable helpers because they run mutating Git commands, can push or delete remote branches, and can create worktrees at custom or config-controlled paths. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious network callbacks, or prompt injection text.

remediation.issue: Branch finishing can push branches, push tags, and delete remote branches without an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode and require confirmation before git push, tag push, local deletion, or remote deletion unless a clearly named force flag is provided.

remediation.issue: Worktree creation accepts user-supplied or config-derived paths without workspace confinement.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve worktree paths, reject sensitive directories, and require confirmation for absolute paths or parent-directory traversal outside an approved base directory.

remediation.issue: Git refs and config-controlled branch names are passed to Git commands without centralized validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate branch and tag names with git check-ref-format and add end-of-options separators where Git subcommands support them.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes global Git configuration and cleanup examples that can affect a user environment.
remediation.suggestion: Label global configuration and cleanup snippets as manual examples, and tell users to inspect affected paths and branches before running them.

semantic_findings.title: Unconfirmed Remote Branch Mutation
semantic_findings.description: The branch finishing workflow pushes target branches and tags to origin, then deletes the remote source branch without an explicit confirmation step in that command path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code directly calls git push and git push origin --delete during finish_branch. This is intended release automation, but it can change remote repository state with the user credentials.

content.user_title: Manage Git Branches with Flow Automation
content.value_statement: Teams lose time when branch names, merge paths, and release flows are inconsistent. This skill provides guided Git branch strategy, validation, and worktree workflows for safer collaboration.
actual_capabilities: Explains Gitflow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, trunk-based, and simple branching strategies.
Generates branch naming guidance with prefixes, issue references, and length rules.
Provides helper scripts for branch creation, branch finishing, cleanup, and configuration.
Validates branch names, merge targets, and flow compliance against project configuration.
Guides Git worktree creation, cleanup, and parallel branch workflows.
Includes configuration templates for several team and release models.
limitations: Git operations depend on the current repository state and local user credentials.
The helper scripts do not replace branch protection rules in the Git hosting service.
Automated cleanup can delete merged local or remote branches when users confirm or pass skip flags.
Worktree paths should be reviewed before running commands in untrusted repositories.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Branching
use_cases.description: Select a branching model, document branch types, and create a shared configuration for a development team.

use_cases.title: Prepare Releases and Hotfixes
use_cases.description: Create release or hotfix branches, validate merge targets, tag releases, and coordinate cleanup steps.

use_cases.title: Work Across Parallel Tasks
use_cases.description: Use Git worktrees to review pull requests or fix urgent bugs without disturbing current feature work.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Branching Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Git branching strategy for my project. Ask about team size, release frequency, deployment style, and required environments before choosing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Daily feature work with branch naming rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a feature branch for this issue. Check the current strategy, suggest the branch name, and list the Git steps I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Merge Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review whether this source branch should merge into this target branch under our configured flow. Explain any naming or policy problems.

prompt_templates.title: Design Worktree Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe worktree workflow for urgent hotfixes and pull request reviews. Include cleanup rules, confirmation points, and path constraints.

output_examples.input: We need a hotfix while my feature branch has local changes.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends creating an isolated hotfix worktree from main, keeping the feature directory unchanged, then merging the fix back through the configured release path.

output_examples.input: Can feature/auth merge directly to main in our Gitflow repo?
output_examples.output: The skill flags this as the wrong target for Gitflow and recommends merging the feature branch to develop before release preparation.

output_examples.input: Set up branch rules for a small continuous deployment team.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends GitHub Flow, short-lived feature branches, pull requests to main, status checks, and automatic branch deletion after merge.

best_practices: Confirm the repository strategy before creating, merging, or deleting branches.
Run dry-run or status checks before cleanup commands that remove branches or worktrees.
Keep worktree directories in a predictable project area and review custom paths first.
anti_patterns: Do not run branch cleanup on an unfamiliar repository without checking merged branches first.
Do not bypass pull requests or branch protection rules for protected branches.
Do not place worktrees in sensitive directories or broad home-directory locations.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and helper scripts. Users should review commands before running operations that push, merge, delete, or create worktrees.

faq.question: Which branching strategies are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Gitflow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, trunk-based development, and a simple single-branch flow.

faq.question: Can it enforce branch protection in GitHub?
faq.answer: It can recommend policies and validate local flow rules, but hosting-level branch protection must be configured in the Git service.

faq.question: Does it support Git worktrees?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains worktree patterns and includes a helper script for creating, listing, removing, and cleaning worktrees.

faq.question: Is it safe for production repositories?
faq.answer: It can be useful for production repositories, but destructive operations should require review, clean working trees, and protected branch policies.
